title: Hard cases: negative words, negative questions and inversion
intro: Read this before the difficult quiz. These traps hide in the helper, not in the main verb.

blocks.title: five checks
items: 1. Find the FIRST helper, or add do / does / did if there is none.
2. In a question put it before the subject. In a negative put **not** after it.
3. After do / does / did the verb is the **base form**: no -s, no -ed, no participle.
5. If a question word is the subject, use **no helper**.

blocks.title: negative words
items: **some** becomes **any** in negatives and questions: I don't have **any** money. Do you have **any** money?
**One negative only:** I don't see **anybody**, or I see **nobody**. Not *I don't see nobody*.
never, nobody, nothing, no, none and hardly are already negative, so they never take n't or not: She has **never** been. Not *She hasn't never been*.

blocks.title: negative questions
items: The short form travels with the helper, in front of the subject: **Isn't** she coming? **Haven't** you finished? **Hadn't** they left?
The formal version keeps **not** after the subject: **Is she not** coming? **Have you not** finished? Both versions mean the same.
Only the helper moves: **Hadn't** she **been** waiting?

blocks.title: inversion after negative adverbs
items: A negative adverb at the front of a sentence pulls the helper in front of the subject, as in a question: **Never have** I seen such a crowd. **Seldom do** we eat out.
**Hardly had** she sat down when the phone rang. **Not only did** he sing, he also danced.
Do / does / did are added if there is no other helper: **Rarely did** he complain.

builds: Question words, subject questions and short answers
